newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines expects $7 bln from overseas workers.
newsitem.headline: Philippines expects $7 bln from overseas workers.

text.p: The Philippines is projecting a $7-billion inflow this year from its overseas contract workers, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Monday.
Singson told reporters the projection was significantly higher than last year's total inflow of $4.9 billion.
The Central Bank's gross international reserves have increased to $11.43 billion as of September 23 due to its massive dollar buying in the foreign exchange market, he added.
Remittances from overseas workers in the first six months of the year totalled $3.479 billion, 57.35 percent higher than the year-ago figure of $2.211 billion.
The influx of foreign exchange from abroad should ease the country's current account position, despite a gaping merchandise trade deficit, Singson added.
The dollar flow from Filipino migrants also boosted the country's first half gross national product to 7.06 percent.
Most of the remittances in the first half of this year came from the United States which totalled $2.672 billion.
About four million Filipinos work abroad.
